newsitem.title: USA: Owens to buy Fibreboard in $600 mln deal. [CORRECTED 15:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Owens to buy Fibreboard in $600 mln deal. [CORRECTED 15:35 GMT]

text.p: Owens Corning said Wednesday it had agreed to acquire Fibreboard Corp for $55 cash per share. An Owens spokesman said the deal was valued at $515 (Corrects from $522) million, or $600 (Corrects from $635) million including debt.
The spokesman said Owens would acquire Fibreboard's 9.5 million outstanding shares, and the transaction was expected to close in early July.
In a statement, the companies said the merger is expected to be accretive to Owens earnings in 1997, excluding non-recurring fees.
Owens Corning said it will make a tender offer for Fibreboard shares, subject to customary conditions, by June 3. Fibreboard would become a wholly owned subsidiary.

Owens Corning said the transaction would be financed using a long-term bank credit facility underwritten by a major financial institution. The company said it remains committed to maintaining its investment grade credit ratings and intends to implement capital structure modifications to achieve that objective.

Owens Corning said the merger, its sixteenth acquisition during the past three years and the largest to date, will strengthen the company's offering in building materials systems and provide Fibreboard the resources for continued growth.

"Merging Fibreboard's businesses with Owens Corning will substantially strengthen our offering of building materials systems and make us a major producer and marketer of vinyl siding, one of the fastest growing products in the building materials market," said Owens Corning chairman and chief executive Glen Hiner.
Building materials producer Owens Corning had 1996 sales of $3.8 billion, the company said.

Fibreboard, a producer of vinyl siding and other residential and industrial building materials had sales in 1996 of $469 million. The company said that on a pro-forma basis -- assuming Fibreboard's 1997 acquisitions had been completed on January 1, 1997 -- the company's sales this year would be expected to be close to $800 million.
